name: Uzziah
overview: Uzziah was a male Levite belonging to the Kohathite clan, identified uniquely as the son of Uriel. His lineage places him within the tribe of Levi, a tribe set apart for priestly and temple duties. The designation Kohathite indicates his ancestral connection to one of the main Levitical families responsible for specific religious functions.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Uzziah' means 'YHWH is [my] strength,' reflecting a recognition of God's sustaining power. He was also known as 'Azariah,' which means 'YHWH has helped,' underscoring divine assistance. Both names emphasize reliance on the Lord, though neither is indicated as being directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Uzziah as the son of Uriel. Additionally, he is inferred to be the son of Shaul and Jonathan, suggesting a lineage within the Levitical family. These relationships highlight his place within a priestly heritage but do not extend beyond these familial connections.
scriptureSignificance: Uzziah's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his Levitical heritage and role within the Kohathite clan, which held important responsibilities in the worship life of Israel. Being the son of Uriel situates him within a notable priestly family, contributing to the temple service and religious order. His dual names, both affirming God's strength and help, reflect a life grounded in dependence on the Lord, consistent with the spiritual identity of the Levites.
